note:
Pick up: connectivity_status self-probe deadlock fix.

Problem: connectivity._http_probe uses sync urllib.request.urlopen inside the async sovereign-sse event loop. SSE self-probe deadlocks (event loop blocked on urlopen, can't serve own /health). Bridge probe also times out from inside sovereign-sse despite being a separate process. Result: connectivity_status reports sse + bridge as DEGRADED with http_error=socket:timed_out, while public stack.templetwo.com/api/heartbeat returns 200 OK and tools work fine.

Why it matters now: HQ-pulse (~/bin/hq-pulse.py, launchd com.templetwo.hq-pulse, every 15 min) reads connectivity_status output and surfaces 'sse DEGRADED' / 'bridge DEGRADED' on every run. During the current mid-upgrade those alerts are largely false positives. Diagnostic-only bug — services are fine — but it makes HQ-pulse a noisy reporter.

Fix shape (~30 min including test):
  (a) Special-case self-probe in _http_probe — if probe URL targets the running process's own port, skip the HTTP call and return OK because the responding tool call itself proves the service is alive.
  (b) Switch _http_probe to async httpx (already a dependency) so probes don't block the event loop and run in parallel.
  Both is best.

Files:
  src/sovereign_stack/connectivity.py:_http_probe (~line 179)
  src/sovereign_stack/connectivity_tools.py:_do_connectivity_status

Verify: from a separate Python process check_all returns ok for sse + bridge (tested 2026-04-28). From inside sovereign-sse via MCP both return degraded with socket timeout. Existing open thread already documents this — search recall_insights for 'connectivity self-probe' or get_open_threads for the entry tagged [sovereign_stack,connectivity,probes,async,event-loop,bug,easy-fix].

After fix: HQ-pulse will start reporting accurate per-service health. No client-side change needed there.
